# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 78 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 78 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_078_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8, Chapter 1

**1** He showed me a great willow tree overshadowing plains and mountains, and under the shade of the willow had gathered all those who are called by the name of the Lord. **2** A glorious and very tall angel of the Lord stood beside the willow, holding a great sickle; he was cutting branches from the willow and distributing them to the people sheltered under the willow, giving each a small rod of about a cubit in length. **3** After all had received their rods, the angel laid down his sickle, and the tree remained intact, just as I had seen it before. **4** I marveled inwardly, saying, "How can the tree be sound after so many branches were cut from it?" The shepherd said to me, "Do not wonder that the tree has remained sound after having so many branches cut off. Wait until you have seen everything, and what it means will be shown to you." **5** The angel who had given the rods to the people then requested them back; and they were summoned to him in the same order in which each had received a rod, and each one returned his rod. **6** The angel of the Lord took them and examined them. From some he received rods that were withered and moth-eaten; he commanded those who had returned rods in that condition to stand aside. **7** Others returned their rods withered but not moth-eaten; these also were commanded to stand aside. **8** Others returned their rods half-withered; these also stood aside. **9** Others returned rods that were half-withered and cracked; these too stood aside. **10** Others returned rods that were green but cracked; these also stood aside. **11** Others returned rods that were half-green and half-withered; these also stood aside. **12** Others brought rods that were two-thirds green and one-third withered; these also stood aside. **13** Others returned rods that were two-thirds withered and one-third green; these also stood aside. **14** Others returned rods that were nearly all green, with only a very little part withered — just at the tip; these stood aside. **15** The rods of still others were completely green; these stood aside, and the angel greatly rejoiced over them, and the shepherd also rejoiced.

---

*LOGOS maintains formal register. The systematic enumeration of rod conditions (vv. 6-15) reflects the original's careful taxonomy of spiritual states.*
